citations.quote: In practical applications, the performance of SIBs under the low-temperature conditions has attracted more attention. Similarly, based on the actual use of SIBs, the impact of different electrolytes on the low-temperature performance of SIBs was also characterized by measuring the cycle performance and rate performance at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , as well as the rate and discharge performance at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Similar to high-temperature performance of pouch cells, these "hard-soft synergy" functional electrolytes induce amazing low-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs. As shown in the Figs 4a, 4b and S5a, both pouch cells with the NB or NP electrolyte can improve the cycling performance compared to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, an excellent capacity retention of $95\%$ after 350 cycles and high stability can be obtained benefiting from the "hard-soft synergy". Notably, though the capacity of the cells with NP or NB electrolyte both over $850\mathrm{mAh}$ (NB-859 mAh vs. NP-850 mAh) after 300 cycles, the NP group shows more fluctuant coulombic efficiency than the NB group, as shown in Fig. 4b. Additionally, the charge/discharge curves of the cells with NP, NB, and baseline electrolytes are shown in Fig. 4c. With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

citations.quote: The electrolytes were prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ) in tetrahydrofuran (THF), 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME), or mixed solvents of THF and DME at different volumetric ratios. The compositions were as follows: pure DME (TD01), THF:DME = 3:7 (TD37), 5:5 (TD55), 7:3 (TD73), and pure THF (TD10). citations.quote:
4. Conclusions
In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries. That is because the formation of compact, stable, and effective SEI film on the surface of the cathode material after adding ADN as electrolyte additive. This work offers an insightful guidance for the practical application of high-performance cathode materials in sodium-ion batteries.

$Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min. Then, the pouch cells were punctuated in vacuum to remove excess electrolyte and gas generated by the side reactions during the charge process. Eventually, the cells were packaged again and cut the air-bags to obtain the finished batteries for testing.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

Before the electrochemical tests, the pouch cells were subjected to a overnight aging and formation treatment. citations.quote: In practical applications, the performance of SIBs under the low-temperature conditions has attracted more attention. Similarly, based on the actual use of SIBs, the impact of different electrolytes on the low-temperature performance of SIBs was also characterized by measuring the cycle performance and rate performance at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , as well as the rate and discharge performance at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Similar to high-temperature performance of pouch cells, these "hard-soft synergy" functional electrolytes induce amazing low-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs. As shown in the Figs 4a, 4b and S5a, both pouch cells with the NB or NP electrolyte can improve the cycling performance compared to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, an excellent capacity retention of $95\%$ after 350 cycles and high stability can be obtained benefiting from the "hard-soft synergy". Notably, though the capacity of the cells with NP or NB electrolyte both over $850\mathrm{mAh}$ (NB-859 mAh vs. NP-850 mAh) after 300 cycles, the NP group shows more fluctuant coulombic efficiency than the NB group, as shown in Fig. 4b. Additionally, the charge/discharge curves of the cells with NP, NB, and baseline electrolytes are shown in Fig. 4c. With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child3
citations.quote: With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling. Besides, rate performance of pouch cells is also improved by the synergistic effect of NP or NB electrolyte even at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , as shown in Fig. 4d and S5b. Furthermore, to evaluate dual additive potential at tougher low-temperatures, $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ discharge tests are necessary. Fig. 4e shows the capacity retention of pouch cells at different discharge currents, revealing the cells all can exhibit good electrochemical performance under the tested temperature conditions. Even at $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $1\mathrm{C}$ , the discharge capacity of pouch cells with NP and NB electrolytes still achieves $729\mathrm{mAh}$ and $697\mathrm{mAh}$ , respectively. These results confirm that this co-additive addition strategy improves extremely low temperature performance of NFM/HC pouch cells. Summarily, compared to single additive or baseline electrolyte, NFM/HC pouch cells with multi-component functional electrolyte possess much better performance. Therein, the cells containing NP electrolyte have better room and high-temperature performance, and the cells containing NB electrolyte are more suitable for low-temperature application.

citations.quote: $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min.

citations.quote:
4. Conclusions
In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries. That is because the formation of compact, stable, and effective SEI film on the surface of the cathode material after adding ADN as electrolyte additive. This work offers an insightful guidance for the practical application of high-performance cathode materials in sodium-ion batteries.

evidence_ledger.quote: In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. evidence_ledger.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

4. Conclusions
In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries. That is because the formation of compact, stable, and effective SEI film on the surface of the cathode material after adding ADN as electrolyte additive. This work offers an insightful guidance for the practical application of high-performance cathode materials in sodium-ion batteries.

2.2 Battery Assembly
$Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min. Then, the pouch cells were punctuated in vacuum to remove excess electrolyte and gas generated by the side reactions during the charge process. Eventually, the cells were packaged again and cut the air-bags to obtain the finished batteries for testing.

evidence_ledger.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
evidence_ledger.paper_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o
evidence_ledger.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

2.1. Preparation of the functional electrolytes and batteries
The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and

TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode. The HC active material, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), and conductive carbon black (Super P) with a mass ratio of 95:1.5:2:1.5 were mixed and dispersed in water, and then the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the HC anode. The areal loading of the anode and cathode were 16.0 g m $^{-2}$ and 33.0 g m $^{-2}$ , respectively. The semi-finished pouch cells were dried under vacuum at 80 °C for 72 h before being moved into a glove box for injecting electrolyte. The size of prepared pouch cells was 52 mm × 5 mm × 100 mm.

That is because the formation of compact, stable, and effective SEI film on the surface of the cathode material after adding ADN as electrolyte additive. This work offers an insightful guidance for the practical application of high-performance cathode materials in sodium-ion batteries.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child2
citations.quote: In practical applications, the performance of SIBs under the low-temperature conditions has attracted more attention. Similarly, based on the actual use of SIBs, the impact of different electrolytes on the low-temperature performance of SIBs was also characterized by measuring the cycle performance and rate performance at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , as well as the rate and discharge performance at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Similar to high-temperature performance of pouch cells, these "hard-soft synergy" functional electrolytes induce amazing low-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs. As shown in the Figs 4a, 4b and S5a, both pouch cells with the NB or NP electrolyte can improve the cycling performance compared to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, an excellent capacity retention of $95\%$ after 350 cycles and high stability can be obtained benefiting from the "hard-soft synergy". Notably, though the capacity of the cells with NP or NB electrolyte both over $850\mathrm{mAh}$ (NB-859 mAh vs. NP-850 mAh) after 300 cycles, the NP group shows more fluctuant coulombic efficiency than the NB group, as shown in Fig. 4b. Additionally, the charge/discharge curves of the cells with NP, NB, and baseline electrolytes are shown in Fig. 4c. With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

citations.quote: S12). As shown in Fig. 2f, at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the TD73 battery had a specific capacity of $99.1\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ and consistent cycling performance, with a retention rate of $88.3\%$ after 100 cycles. However, the full cell with TD01 performs poorly at low temperatures, with an initial specific capacity of only $87.5\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , and rapid capacity decay with increasing cycles. This clearly shows that the inclusion of THF improves the performance of ether-based electrolytes at low temperature. It improves the stability of both layered oxide cathodes and HC anodes, while the assembled full cells also exhibit excellent electrochemical performance. To examine the interfacial dynamics of the electrolyte at low temperature, we analyzed the half-cell impedance data following 50 cycles at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The results indicated that TD73 demonstrated lower interfacial resistance (53.8 $\Omega$ ), while TD01 recorded a value of $64.11\Omega$ (Fig. 3a). The results demonstrate that the incorporation of THF diminishes the interfacial barrier and enhances reaction kinetics at low temperature. Furthermore, we examined the impedance variations of the TD73 half-cell from $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The Arrhenius equation $(\frac{1}{R_{ct}} = Aexp\left(\frac{-E_a}{RT}\right))$ allows for the calculation of activation energy through the fitting of impedance at various temperature.

citations.quote:
4. Conclusions
In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries. That is because the formation of compact, stable, and effective SEI film on the surface of the cathode material after adding ADN as electrolyte additive. This work offers an insightful guidance for the practical application of high-performance cathode materials in sodium-ion batteries.

2.2 Battery Assembly
$Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min. Then, the pouch cells were punctuated in vacuum to remove excess electrolyte and gas generated by the side reactions during the charge process. Eventually, the cells were packaged again and cut the air-bags to obtain the finished batteries for testing.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. 4. Conclusions
In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries. That is because the formation of compact, stable, and effective SEI film on the surface of the cathode material after adding ADN as electrolyte additive. This work offers an insightful guidance for the practical application of high-performance cathode materials in sodium-ion batteries.

citations.quote: In practical applications, the performance of SIBs under the low-temperature conditions has attracted more attention. Similarly, based on the actual use of SIBs, the impact of different electrolytes on the low-temperature performance of SIBs was also characterized by measuring the cycle performance and rate performance at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , as well as the rate and discharge performance at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and $-30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Similar to high-temperature performance of pouch cells, these "hard-soft synergy" functional electrolytes induce amazing low-temperature performance of NFM/HC SIBs. As shown in the Figs 4a, 4b and S5a, both pouch cells with the NB or NP electrolyte can improve the cycling performance compared to the cells with the baseline electrolyte, an excellent capacity retention of $95\%$ after 350 cycles and high stability can be obtained benefiting from the "hard-soft synergy". Notably, though the capacity of the cells with NP or NB electrolyte both over $850\mathrm{mAh}$ (NB-859 mAh vs. NP-850 mAh) after 300 cycles, the NP group shows more fluctuant coulombic efficiency than the NB group, as shown in Fig. 4b. Additionally, the charge/discharge curves of the cells with NP, NB, and baseline electrolytes are shown in Fig. 4c. With the help of "hard-soft synergy", polarization and capacity fading are alleviated signally during the cycling.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

As shown in Fig. 2f, at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ , the TD73 battery had a specific capacity of $99.1\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ and consistent cycling performance, with a retention rate of $88.3\%$ after 100 cycles. However, the full cell with TD01 performs poorly at low temperatures, with an initial specific capacity of only $87.5\mathrm{mAhg}^{-1}$ , and rapid capacity decay with increasing cycles. This clearly shows that the inclusion of THF improves the performance of ether-based electrolytes at low temperature. To examine the interfacial dynamics of the electrolyte at low temperature, we analyzed the half-cell impedance data following 50 cycles at $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The results demonstrate that the incorporation of THF diminishes the interfacial barrier and enhances reaction kinetics at low temperature. Furthermore, we examined the impedance variations of the TD73 half-cell from $-20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . The Arrhenius equation $(\frac{1}{R_{ct}} = Aexp\left(\frac{-E_a}{RT}\right))$ allows for the calculation of activation energy through the fitting of impedance at various temperature.

citations.quote:
4. Conclusions
In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries. That is because the formation of compact, stable, and effective SEI film on the surface of the cathode material after adding ADN as electrolyte additive. This work offers an insightful guidance for the practical application of high-performance cathode materials in sodium-ion batteries.

2.2 Battery Assembly
$Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ , carbon nanotubes (CNTs), polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and carbon black with the mass ratio of 92.5: 2.0: 3.5: 2.0 were mixed in pyrrolidone to form a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 14 um thick aluminum foil to prepare the cathode electrode. The areal density was measured to be 10.0 mg cm $^{-2}$ , and the compacted density was 2.1 g cm $^{-3}$ . To prepare the anode electrode, hard carbon (Kuraray), carbon black, cellulose sodium (CMC), and styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) with the mass ratio of 94.5: 1.0: 2.0: 2.5 were added in deionized water and stirred into a uniform slurry, and then coated on a 9 um thick copper foil with the areal and compacted densities of 4.31 mg cm $^{-2}$ and 1.4 g cm $^{-3}$ , respectively. The cathode, anode, and separator (20 μm polypropylene) were assembled into pouch cells with a designed capacity of 650 mAh, and the thickness, width, and length were 10, 68, and 127 mm, respectively. The cells were dried in vacuum (-99 kPa/80 °C) until the water content was less than 150 ppm. At a dewpoint of -40 °C, the electrolytes defined as G1, G2, G3, and G4 (Table 1) were injected into the cells. After packaging in vacuum at room temperature for 48 hours; the pouch cells were placed at the environment with 0.8 MPa and 45 °C and charged at 0.05 C for 180 min, followed by another charge at a constant current of 0.1 C for 360 min. Then, the pouch cells were punctuated in vacuum to remove excess electrolyte and gas generated by the side reactions during the charge process. Eventually, the cells were packaged again and cut the air-bags to obtain the finished batteries for testing.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

citations.chunk_id: 0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2
citations.quote:
ABSTRACT
A “hard-soft synergy” strategy is firstly developed to design functional multi-component electrolytes and successfully achieve drastic temperature performance of $NaNi_{0.33}Fe_{0.33}Mn_{0.33}O_{2}$ (NFM)/hard carbon (HC) sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) over a wide range from $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ to $60\ ^{\circ}C$ . Coupling “hard”-sodium difluorophosphate (NaDFP) with “soft”-tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphate (TMSP) or tris(trimethylsilyl) borate (TMSB) reasonably realizes an optimized solvation structure from “solvent dominated” to “anion collaborative” and synergistic-formed tough and multi-component interfacial films. Benefit to these, the cycling stability is considerably improved under the room and cold conditions, the capacity retention after 350 cycles increases from 0 % to 92 % and even stable cycling performance at 1 C (1 C = 900 mA) can be obtained at $-10\ ^{\circ}C$ . Discharge capacity at $-30\ ^{\circ}C$ and the capacity retention after storage at $60\ ^{\circ}C$ are also greatly improved. Furthermore, the functional mechanisms of different electrolyte combinations under extreme temperature conditions are analyzed. It is demonstrated that the combination of NaDFP and TMSP is more suitable for high-temperature requirements due to its tougher cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI), reduced transition metal dissolution, and minimized cathode phase deviation. In contrast, the combination of NaDFP and TMSB is more suitable for low-temperature requirements, benefiting from the reduced desolvation energy and viscosity. In addition to the obtained functional electrolytes, this work also provides new insight for designing functional multi-component electrolytes of SIBs.

Summarily, compared to single additive or baseline electrolyte, NFM/HC pouch cells with multi-component functional electrolyte possess much better performance. 4. Conclusions
In summary, a commercially feasible sodium-ion pouch cell with $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ /hard carbon is fabricated in this work. According to the calculation of the frontier molecular orbital energy, the electrolyte additive adiponitrile (ADN) is selected as the electrolyte additive to improve the performance of sodium-ion battery for the first time, and the effects of the ADN on the performance improvement of the cathode material $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ are investigated for the first time. The results show that ADN can promote the formation of highly conductive and stable SEI film on the cathode material surface, and effectively improve the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of $Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_{2}$ as the cathode electrode material of sodium-ion batteries. In particular, the battery with 3% ADN shows the most obvious improvement, its discharge capacity increases by 10.5%, 8%, and 13% at the operating temperature of 45, -10, and -20 °C, respectively. For the cycling stability, the capacity retention rate of the battery without adding ADN drops rapidly to 75% after 40 cycles, while the capacity retention rate of the battery with 3% ADN can still reach 78% after 220 cycles. Adding ADN as electrolyte additive effectively improves the electrochemical performance of sodium ion batteries. That is because the formation of compact, stable, and effective SEI film on the surface of the cathode material after adding ADN as electrolyte additive. This work offers an insightful guidance for the practical application of high-performance cathode materials in sodium-ion batteries.

association_citations.quote: The improvement need to be verified in sodium ion battery [20-21]. Considering the practical application of sodium-ion batteries, the cost-effective ternary layered $\mathrm{Na_{0.76}Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.4}Mn_{0.3}O_2}$ and commercial hard carbon were used as the cathode and anode materials, respectively, and 1.0 M NaPF $_6$ in the mixed solvent of EC: DEC: PC was used as the electrolyte, with FEC as the basic additive. A sodium-ion pouch cell with the capacity of 650 mAh was assembled, and the effect of ADN on the high-low-temperature performance and cycling stability of the cathode material Na $_{0.76}$ Ni $_{0.3}$ Fe $_{0.4}$ Mn $_{0.3}$ O $_2$ were electrochemically investigated in detail. Moreover, the effects of the electrolyte additive ADN on the formation of SEI film on the surface of the cathode material were studied by spectroscopic analyses.

review.recommendation_reason: The candidate's composition and full-cell format are matched in the literature, but the source reports no initial Coulombic efficiency for any group, and the candidate is the no-ADN baseline whose improvements in the paper are attributed to ADN; with no computation results recorded, there is insufficient evidence to recommend this candidate as an ICE-improving intervention, so a held decision is warranted.

## 配方筛选结果 已整理候选资料，当前暂缓推荐。未满足的条件列在下方。 ### 候选资料：same-paper-1（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaPF6；溶剂：EC, EMC；溶剂比例（基准待核对）：EC=0.3, EMC=0.7；添加剂：NaDFP。 - 配方原文 [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0]：The main raw materials used for preparing functional electrolytes, including EC, EMC, $NaPF_{6}$ , NaDFP, TMSP and TMSB were provided by the Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology Co, Ltd. The baseline electrolyte was prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ in a mixture of EC: EMC=3:7 to form a concentration of 0.8 mol $L^{-1}$ . Then, NaDFP was added into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the NaDFP electrolyte, and NaDFP and TMSB or TMSP were respectively added into the baseline electrolyte and assigned as NB or NP electrolyte. All electrolytes were prepared in a dry argon filled glove box with both moisture and oxygen concentrations below 0.1 ppm. NFM was purchased from Jiangsu Xiangying New Energy Technology Co, Ltd, HC was purchased from Kuraray Co Ltd. The pouch test cells with NFM cathode (120 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.1 C), HC anode (290 mAh g $^{-1}$ at 0.05 C), and Celgard 2700 separator were assembled using the conventional assembly method. Therein, NFM active material, polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF), carbon nanotube (CNT), conductive carbon black (Super P), and Maleic acid (the reason of addition maleic acid was shown in Table 1) were dispersed in N-methylpyrrolidone (NMP) with a mass ratio of 94.5:1.8:1:2.5:0.2, and the slurry was coated on an aluminum substrate to prepare the NFM cathode. ### 候选资料：lit-td73-0178（尚未获推荐） 以下为候选记录中的组成，配制时须核对所引原文的比例基准与用量。 盐：NaPF6；浓度：1 mol L⁻¹；NaPF6：1 mol L⁻¹；溶剂：THF, DME；溶剂比例（体积）：THF=0.7, DME=0.3。 - 配方原文 [0178_Zeng 等 - 2026 - Weak-interaction ether-based electrolyte towards stable operation of low-temperature sodium-ion batt::sec7::child0]：The electrolytes were prepared by dissolving $NaPF_{6}$ (1 mol L $^{-1}$ ) in tetrahydrofuran (THF), 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME), or mixed solvents of THF and DME at different volumetric ratios. ## 候选评估 ### same-paper-1 评估建议：The candidate's composition matches the paper's NaDFP electrolyte, but the paper provides no NaDFP-specific evidence for improving ICE after formation at -20 C and indicates that the dual-additive NB/NP electrolytes are the ones with enhanced wide-temperature performance, so the current-task evidence does not support recommending this candidate. 任务要求与已有依据（模型语义判断，程序核验出处）： - Electrolyte formulation is NaPF6 dissolved in an EC:EMC = 3:7 solvent mixture (candidate identity).：The paper states the baseline electrolyte is NaPF6 in EC:EMC=3:7 at 0.8 mol/L, which matches the candidate's salt/solvent/ratio. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0] - The intervention is the NaDFP additive in the baseline electrolyte (candidate identity).：The paper describes adding NaDFP into the baseline electrolyte to prepare the 'NaDFP electrolyte', exactly the candidate's single-additive composition. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0] - Target cell format: hard-carbon anode || layered-oxide (NFM) cathode sodium-ion pouch full cell.：The paper assembles NFM/HC pouch cells (NFM cathode, HC anode, pouch test cells), matching the required full-cell chemistry and format. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0] - Improves initial Coulombic efficiency after formation for this candidate.：The paper only notes that first-cycle Coulombic efficiencies differ across additives and that the film-forming process changed, and it concludes NB and NP electrolytes are expected to outperform the baseline and NaDFP-containing electrolytes; it gives no NaDFP-specific ICE improvement value after formation. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec7::child8] - Performance benefit at -20 C for this candidate.：-20 C tests are reported, but the low-temperature benefit is attributed to the dual-additive NB (and NP) electrolytes; NaDFP-containing electrolyte is described as inferior to NB/NP, and no NaDFP-alone -20 C metric tied to ICE is reported. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec8::child2][0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec2] 文献与候选的关联：The candidate maps to the paper's 'NaDFP electrolyte' (baseline NaPF6/EC:EMC 3:7 plus NaDFP) tested in NFM/HC pouch full cells; this identity match supports evaluating the candidate against the paper's formed-cell results, but the paper's favorable findings are mainly attached to the dual-additive NB/NP variants rather than NaDFP alone. [0156_Cai 等 - 2025 - A hard-soft synergy strategy enables drastic temperature performance of pouch sodium-ion batteries o::sec4::child0] ### lit-td73-0178 评估建议：The candidate's identity (1 M NaPF6 in THF:DME 7:3) and a -20 °C hard-carbon||layered-oxide full-cell test are documented, but the decisive target metric—initial Coulombic efficiency after formation—is not reported for this candidate, and the reported cells are CR2025 coin cells rather than pouch cells.
